title: Effective readonly stack is rejected as writable
observed: Known successful Bridges v1 memory mount evidence has hidden lower rw and upper ro at the same path, with actual statvfs ST_RDONLY set. mount_for max(tuple) selects rw by lexicographic options on equal paths, and main separately rejects every hidden rw row. Both prevent pytest from starting on that valid layout.
reproduction: test_B1_known_effective_ro_stack_is_falsely_rejected; actual50316939 memory lines/read_only evidence, no real container launched.
minimal_fix: Check effective declared readonly mount targets using actual path flags or correctly resolved topmost mount IDs; do not reject hidden lower mounts. Keep raw mount evidence and the intended readonly guard; do not weaken it to a bind-string assertion.

title: Budget can expire during log opening before Popen
observed: Last allocation/clock decision occurs before opening stdout/stderr. Advancing time past the phase deadline while opening pytest.stdout still calls Popen; only afterward is timed_out recorded.
reproduction: test_B2_expired_after_log_open_still_launches: fake clock601 after deadline600, one Popen call, no real child launched.
minimal_fix: After final prelaunch I/O, immediately recheck/clamp actual allocation and wall/monotonic budget before Popen; refuse expired launch without increasing an existing deadline.

title: Cleanup failure resets a second full grace period
observed: cleanup_group called normally may exhaust15TERM+5KILL/reap and raise; execute_phase except calls cleanup_group again, resetting the full budget. This exceeds the claimed one20second cleanup allowance.
reproduction: test_B3_cleanup_error_restarts_cleanup_budget observes2cleanup invocations when the first cleanup raises.
minimal_fix: Use one shared absolute cleanup budget or do not restart grace after cleanup itself failed. Preserve primary and cleanup error evidence and retain best-effort KILL/reap within that single bound.
